metadata.reviewed_source: Actual working files; SHA-256 per source captured in baseline_repro_results.json. Local HEAD lagged the requested core commit.
metadata.live_trading: DISABLED; no live order, wallet or signing action performed
metadata.integration_assessment: Changes requested: resolve the identified accounting/state/risk/operations defects before claiming the corresponding guarantees. This is not financial authorization or an execution audit.

findings.title: Restore accepts states that violate funding, type, and risk invariants
findings.observed: With an unchanged legitimate config hash and no fills, changing saved cash from 100 to 101 is accepted. Negative risk count=-100 and fees=-100 are accepted. pending='false' is accepted as truthy and buys on otherwise flat trend data. version=True is accepted as version 1.
findings.effect: An invalid export or edited, correctly digested journal can introduce unsupported capital, waive daily limits, or create a signal that the strategy never generated. The outer digest only proves byte consistency; it does not establish a valid ledger. This is a state-validation defect, not a claim that local users with code-write access can be sandboxed.
findings.expected: Strict schema/types and finite bounds; ledger and position reconciliation back to initial external capital; risk counters and pending signal consistent with recorded activity/history. Reject inconsistent state before mutating an engine.
findings.fix: Validate the complete restore schema, including exact integer versions, boolean pending, nonnegative finite risk fields and allowed halt reasons. Reconcile cash + cost_basis = initial_capital + realized_pnl, units, fees, fills and failed-attempt records; do not merely cap current cash at 100 because earned gains are permitted. Validate active/closed trade records and immutable experiment identity.

findings.title: Paper fills use candle-start UTC days for caps despite occurring on observation days
findings.observed: With interval=60 and max_trades_day=1: warm candle ts=86280 at 86341; buy candle ts=86340 at observed_at=86401; sell candle ts=86400 at observed_at=86461. Both fills occurred on observed UTC day 1, yet both pass the one-fill cap. The first fill was charged to risk day 0.
findings.effect: Prospective daily fill and fee limits, day-loss accounting, timestamps and holding periods can describe the wrong execution day. The default cap can likewise gain an extra fill around midnight.
findings.expected: Paper risk, fill time and execution accounting use the validated observation/execution time, while candle identity remains a separate source timestamp. Historical next-open execution retains its actual modeled bar-open time.
findings.fix: Introduce a single explicit execution timestamp: bar.ts for historical next-open fills, observed_at for prospective fills. Use it for daily risk checks/records and trade entry/exit timing; retain source_bar_ts separately. Do not update risk backwards to bar.ts + interval - 1 after a later observed execution.

findings.title: Failed-exit gas is omitted from closed-trade outcomes
findings.observed: Buy 20 USD at price 10; fail one exit; exit at 10.125; fee/slippage zero and gas 0.10 for each attempt. Account ending equity is 99.95 and realized P&L is -0.05, but closed_trade.net_pnl is +0.05 and win_rate is 1.0. Total gas correctly includes all three attempts.
findings.effect: Closed-trade wins, average win/loss and profit factor can report a winning trade whose actual net effect was a loss. Overall account net P&L is correct, which limits but does not remove the misleading trade statistics.
findings.expected: Gas attributable to failed exits of an open trade reduces that trade's net P&L. Failed entries must have an explicit, reconciled treatment as attempt overhead or trade-attributed costs.
findings.fix: Accumulate failed-attempt costs into current_trade when a position is open and keep separate unattributed entry-attempt overhead where appropriate. Assert closed/open trade P&L plus explicit overhead reconciles to portfolio realized/unrealized totals; cover partial exits followed by failure and final exit.

findings.title: Healthy non-minute feeds are halted before another completed candle is due
findings.observed: A four-hour candle ending at 14400 warms at now=14401. Polling exactly the same healthy completed feed at now=14500 returns HALTED_DATA_STALE, although the next four-hour candle will not close until 28800. The CLI defaults to this four-hour interval when no config is supplied.
findings.effect: Most normal observation times immediately halt the default paper command. A healthy source is mistaken for an outage, and the halt is sticky.
findings.expected: Staleness reflects when the next completed bar is expected plus an explicit source-delay allowance, independently of maximum allowed execution-price age.
findings.fix: Derive freshness from interval cadence and expected next completion, with bounded provider grace. If a separate 90-second execution-price-age rule is intended, apply and label it separately rather than calling a still-current completed-bar feed stale.

findings.title: Older overlapping source revisions are silently accepted
findings.observed: Warm bars at ts 0, 60, 120 with close 10. The next feed changes ts 0 close to 11, keeps ts 120 identical, and adds ts 180. paper_step returns PROCESSED_PROSPECTIVE_BAR and fault=None while its journal still retains the old close 10 for ts 0.
findings.effect: One run can silently mix different versions of the same source history. Recomputing the strategy from the newly returned history can differ from the continued journal; the promised conflicting-bar halt only covers the latest cached candle.
findings.expected: All overlapping stored source bars are compared, and any revision becomes a durable data fault without a new fill.
findings.fix: Validate the full overlap by timestamp (or persist sufficient per-bar hashes for retained decision context), not only the most recent bar. Keep source observation identity and the revision reason in the journal.

findings.title: A halted paper result presents old equity alongside a fresh source timestamp
findings.observed: Paper buys 2 units at price 10 with cash 80, then a stale-data fault is set. A subsequent fully validated new close of 1 returns source_last_close=180 and HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW, but ending_equity remains 100 rather than the current mark of 82. The open 2 units remain recorded.
findings.effect: The system correctly retains exposure and does not fake a liquidation, but its headline ending-equity/drawdown metrics can hide losses after a halt unless a consumer inspects the old equity-curve timestamp.
findings.expected: Halting trading does not imply frozen economic value. Mark retained exposure using valid subsequent observations without trading, or explicitly identify the mark as stale with valuation_as_of and unavailable-current-equity semantics.
findings.fix: Separate observation/valuation from order eligibility. Preserve the sticky halt while recording fresh marks, or mark all returned performance figures as stale/as-of. Do not fabricate fills or clear the fault to update valuation.

findings.title: Strategy or implementation changes do not invalidate an existing experiment
findings.observed: Create a trend state with fast=12/slow=48, change the registered trend fast parameter to 2, then restore the state with the same strategy name. Restore succeeds; saved identity includes only schema version, config hash and the name 'trend'.
findings.effect: A changed strategy or engine implementation can continue the same paper journal without an explicit migration/new experiment. The full-period evidence may then combine different rules, violating preregistration and restart reproducibility.
findings.expected: The journal records and verifies immutable strategy parameters and a meaningful engine/build/semantics version, plus the relevant source identity.
findings.fix: Fingerprint the actual frozen strategy specification and engine semantic version/build identity; reject mismatches before any action. Record source provider/request provenance in the durable journal, not only the per-invocation output. A schema version alone cannot substitute for strategy identity.

findings.title: Direct paper API data faults do not persist a halt
findings.observed: Warm a journal whose pending signal is long. A new NaN candle raises ValueError before the journal is locked or updated. Calling paper_step again with the corrected next bar produces a buy and fault=None.
findings.effect: The fail-closed guarantee depends on using the CLI wrapper. A script that uses the public paper_step API and catches an input error can silently resume a previously faulted experiment. The current CLI handler does persist a fault for this case, so this finding does not claim the same bypass through that wrapper.
findings.expected: The persistent paper abstraction itself owns durable fault transitions, and each exposed caller receives the same restart behavior.
findings.fix: Centralize existing-journal fault recording inside the locked paper operation or a shared wrapper used by every entry point. Preserve state integrity/config checks before writing faults; do not handle a concurrent writer's lock denial by overwriting its journal.

findings.title: The paper output path can overwrite its own restart state
findings.observed: Pass the same path to --state and --output. The first mocked-data paper run returns code 0, but the path now contains only continuous_service/live_trading/observations; its engine envelope is gone.
findings.effect: An ordinary argument mistake destroys the authoritative restart journal after a reported successful run. The next invocation cannot restore it.
findings.expected: State and report destinations must be distinct before any writes.
findings.fix: Reject canonical-path collisions before fetching or writing, including equivalent relative paths and existing symlink/hardlink aliases where practical. Keep report writes outside the journal namespace.

findings.title: Historical completion is checked against the wrong or no cutoff
findings.observed: With one-minute rows at 0, 60, 120, fetch_bars(before=120, now=180) returns all three; the last row only became complete at 180, after the intended frozen cutoff 120. Separately, run_backtest accepts year-2100 bars, and the new research runner reads CSV without a now/as-of completion bound. The backtest CLI's read_csv(..., now=time.time()) already demonstrates the correct boundary enforcement pattern.
findings.effect: A frozen historical rerun can admit information unavailable at its cutoff, and the reporting script can produce accepted results from future or incomplete CSV candles.
findings.expected: Dataset completion is validated against the experiment's explicit as-of bound at production entry points; synthetic timeless fixtures are an explicit separate testing mode.
findings.fix: For a frozen as-of request, parse at min(observed_at, requested_cutoff) and record that cutoff in provenance. Pass a current or frozen as-of into research CSV validation and the historical runner contract. Root independently identified the before-cutoff issue during this review; this finding confirms it rather than claiming novel discovery.

nonblocking_notes.title: Historical backtest can be labelled mode=paper
nonblocking_notes.observed: run_backtest(..., Config(mode='paper'), Strategy('trend')) succeeds and reports mode='paper'.
nonblocking_notes.effect: The command remains a historical simulation, but downstream readers should not infer prospective observations from this mode field.
nonblocking_notes.fix: Reject incompatible command/config modes or add an explicit execution_kind='historical_backtest' and separate prospective evidence classification. A 'paper' label alone is never qualified L4 evidence.
